29.​Add after paragraph 127 and renumber (London - Kingston) 
 
The crisis in capitalism has resulted in a crisis of unemployment the worst this 
country has seen since Covid, with an estimated 9 million plus unemployed, 1.65 
million in January 2026 alone seeking benefits and over 700,000 graduates who 
cannot find a job as of January 2026. Alongside this, UK graduate jobs are at their 
lowest since 2012, and there are fewer than 10,000 graduate jobs available on the job 
market. 
 
Students, after years training for an industry at university, will graduate and find 
themselves jobless. This is already the case with younger workers, creating a clear 
feeling amongst young people that any chance at a liveable future has been stolen 
from them and that this system has nothing to offer them. In the absence of a clear 
political alternative at present this primarily manifests itself as cynicism and 
pessimism. However this pessimism does not replace radicalism but often goes 
alongside it, and under the hammer blows of great events this pessimism can turn 
into its opposite in as little as 24 hours, with many drawing revolutionary conclusions.​
 
CC recommendation: Reject 
 
30.​Amend paragraph 139 (Bath) 
 
This contributes to the rise of racist attacks and abuse in society. The youth in particular are 
disgusted by this, and see little difference between Robinson’s hardcore supporters and 
disgruntled workers, who are clumped together by some on the left under the umbrella label 
of ‘far right’ or ‘fascist’. 
 
140. More generally, ‘Culture war’ rhetoric is used as a distraction from the wider 
crisis of capitalism. We should expect similar vitriol to be directed against any 
minority that is sufficiently vulnerable and politically expedient to scapegoat. Our task 
is to recruit young people who are being radicalised over racism the endless attacks 
against minorities; to organise and educate them in our revolutionary programme and 
perspectives; and to provide them with a real solution to the scourge of racism oppression: a 
solution based on radical class-based policies and militant class-struggle methods – 
something that the reformists and sects are organically unable to offer. 
 
Explanation: Proposal is to change paragraph 139 by splitting it in two separate paragraphs 
and amending the second part 
 
CC recommendation: Reject
